venues.name: Mont Cervin Palace
venues.note: The 1852 grande dame at the heart of the village, the address Zermatt is measured against.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Riffelalp Resort 2222m
venues.note: Europe's highest five-star hotel, car-free, reached only by the Gornergrat railway, alone with the Matterhorn.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Grand Hotel Zermatterhof
venues.note: A Belle Époque palace built by the villagers themselves in 1879, old-world grandeur, impeccably kept.

venues.name: The Omnia
venues.note: A minimalist mountain lodge on the rock above the village, reached by a tunnel and lift cut into the mountainside.

venues.name: CERVO Mountain Resort
venues.note: A cluster of chalets at the foot of the Sunnegga slopes, sustainable, stylish and quietly modern.

venues.name: Backstage Hotel Vernissage
venues.note: Artist Heinz Julen's avant-garde design hotel, sculptural, theatrical and unlike anything else in the Alps.
credentials: Home of After Seven, 2 MICHELIN Stars

venues.name: After Seven
venues.note: Ivo Adam's surprise menu cooked in an open kitchen, bread baked at your table, and the village's brightest star.

venues.name: The Omnia
venues.note: Alpine ingredients with a global hand, in the design hotel's cool dining room on the rock above the village.

venues.name: Chez Vrony
venues.note: A century-old family alp above the village, cooking its own organic beef with the Matterhorn full in the window.

venues.name: Findlerhof
venues.note: The other beloved Findeln kitchen, sun-terrace mountain cooking, refined and warmly run.

venues.name: Brasserie Lusi
venues.note: The Zermatterhof's confident brasserie, grand-hotel cooking without the ceremony.

venues.name: Marmo
venues.note: A modern mountain kitchen at Furi, a serious table on the slopes, not just a hut.

venues.name: Bazaar
venues.note: Predominantly vegetarian world flavours, Arab to Chinese, at CERVO's lively base.

venues.name: Aroleid Restaurant
venues.note: Seasonal, honest cooking that quietly won the village's only Bib Gourmand, value done right.

venues.name: Gornergrat Railway
venues.note: The cogwheel train that hauls you from the village up to 3,089m in about 33 minutes, and the whole way the Matterhorn hangs in the window over a fan of glaciers and 4,000m peaks. Book seats on the right for the best of it, and let the little ones and the grandparents ride effortlessly to a view most people only earn on foot. This is the single easiest, most magnificent multi-generation morning in the Alps.
credentials: Highest open-air cogwheel railway in Europe

venues.name: Gornergrat summit & Kulmhotel observatory
venues.note: The top station is a natural balcony ringed by 29 peaks over 4,000m and the vast Gorner Glacier, with the astronomical observatory domes of the Kulmhotel crowning the ridge. The air is thin and the silence total; a private guide can name every summit while you sip something warm. Come for the panorama, stay for the astonishing near-zero-light-pollution night sky.
credentials: Views of 29 peaks above 4,000m including Monte Rosa, the highest in Switzerland

venues.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
venues.note: The highest cable-car station on the continent, where a viewing platform opens onto 38 four-thousanders and 14 glaciers spread across Switzerland, Italy and France. The lift does all the climbing; you simply step out into the roof of Europe. For an Indian family, it is the closest thing to standing on top of the Alps without a rope.

venues.name: The Glacier Palace ice cave
venues.note: A tunnel carved fifteen metres into the living glacier, walls of blue ice, carved sculptures, and a small ice slide the children will beg to repeat. It sits inside the highest cable-car station in Europe, so you fold it into the summit visit. Wrap up warm; the cave holds a steady sub-zero even in a July heatwave.
credentials: World's highest glacier ice palace (inside the 3,883m station)

venues.name: The Cinema Lounge, Klein Matterhorn
venues.note: A small cinema at nearly 3,900m showing short films on the mountains, the glacier and the flora, a gentle place to acclimatise and rest while the body adjusts to the altitude. It is an easy, warm interlude for grandparents between the ice cave and the platform. A quiet reminder that even the roof of Europe can be done in comfort.

venues.name: Matterhorn Glacier Ride (3S cableway)
venues.note: The tri-cable gondola that lifts you the final stretch to the summit station in nine minutes, crystal-studded 'Crystal ride' cabins with glass floors on select cabins that turn transparent over the glacier. It is a thrill in itself, engineering as spectacle. Ask about the crystal cabin for a set-piece the teenagers will film the whole way up.

venues.name: Gornergrat sunrise & Riffelsee special train
venues.note: On set dates the railway runs a dedicated pre-dawn service so you reach the ridge as the first light turns the Matterhorn's east face to fire and doubles it in the Riffelsee. Breakfast follows at the mountain restaurant while the crowds are still asleep in the valley. Pure honeymoon material, and worth the early alarm.

venues.name: Five Lakes Walk (5-Seenweg)
venues.note: A gentle high trail past five alpine lakes, Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, three of which mirror the Matterhorn on a calm day. No exposure, no scrambling, just larch forest, wildflowers and one perfect reflection after another over three to four hours. The most rewarding easy hike above Zermatt for a mixed-ability family.

venues.name: Stellisee lake
venues.note: The wind-sheltered jewel of the Five Lakes Walk and, for many, the finest Matterhorn reflection of all, an unbroken double of the peak on a still summer morning. The Fluhalp mountain restaurant sits a few minutes on for a leisurely lunch with the same view. Go early; by midday a breeze usually ruffles the mirror.

venues.name: Sunnegga & Leisee
venues.note: A three-minute underground funicular from the village lifts you to a sunny terrace and the shallow Leisee, a warm-ish swimming lake with the Matterhorn behind and a lakeside playground, the gentlest of the high viewpoints. Perfect for a family with young children or grandparents who want the view without the walk. The quickest route from village to a first Matterhorn panorama.

venues.name: Rothorn viewpoint
venues.note: The highest of the Sunnegga-side summits, reached by funicular and cable car, with a wide sweep of glaciers and a superb, less-crowded angle on the Matterhorn. It is a spectacular sunrise perch for those who want the golden peak without the Gornergrat crowds. A quiet counterpoint to the busier railway summit.

venues.name: Matterhorn Museum – Zermatlantis
venues.note: An underground reconstructed old village that tells how a poor farming hamlet became the world's most famous mountain, centred on the snapped rope from the 1865 first ascent that killed four of Edward Whymper's seven climbers. Whymper's ice-axe and boots, the church bells, the cobbled lanes, it is moving and beautifully done. The one indoor hour that makes the whole valley make sense.

venues.name: The Hinterdorf old village
venues.note: A cluster of black larch barns, stables and granaries from the 16th to 18th centuries, many raised on stilts topped with round flat 'mouse-stones' to keep rodents out of the grain. A five-minute wander back through Walliser mountain life, wedged among the boutiques. Loveliest in late light when the resinous timber glows almost black.

venues.name: The Kirchbrücke (church bridge) view
venues.note: The little bridge over the Matter Vispa where the whole village funnels the eye straight up to the Matterhorn, the classic street-level shot with chalets, church tower and peak all in one frame. It is a two-minute stroll from the grand hotels and best at first light or blue hour. The picture everyone comes home with.

venues.name: Bahnhofstrasse & luxury shopping
venues.note: The car-free main street lined with Swiss watch houses and jewellers, Bucherer for Rolex, Patek, Chopard and Cartier, alongside ski and cashmere boutiques and chocolatiers. No cars, no fumes, just electric taxis and the Matterhorn at the end of the road. An elegant, unhurried afternoon between mountain excursions.

venues.name: The car-free village stroll
venues.note: Zermatt has banned petrol cars for decades; you arrive by train and move by foot, e-taxi or horse-drawn sleigh, and the air is clean and the streets quiet. That exclusivity, an entire luxury village without traffic, is a large part of its charm for a discerning traveller. Simply walking it in the evening, watching the peak turn pink, is an event in itself.
credentials: One of Europe's original car-free (combustion-free) resorts

venues.name: Gorner Gorge (Gornerschlucht)
venues.note: A narrow slot canyon of 220-million-year-old green serpentine rock, threaded by a timber walkway first built by local guides in the 1880s, with turquoise meltwater roaring below. Fifteen minutes from the centre and blessedly cool on a hot day. A short, dramatic detour that suits a rainy morning or restless children.

venues.name: Chez Vrony, Findeln
venues.note: The most coveted mountain table above Zermatt, a century-old family farm-restaurant on a sun-terrace facing the Matterhorn, serving its own dry-cured meats, alpine cheese and a famous burger from cattle grazed on the slope. Book well ahead; the terrace at lunch is where Zermatt's regulars are. An unhurried, glorious high-altitude lunch with the peak for a backdrop.

venues.name: Fondue & raclette in the village
venues.note: This is the Valais, the home of raclette, and a bubbling caquelon of fondue or a scraped wheel of alpine cheese in a low-beamed stube is the evening ritual after a day on the heights. Ask ahead and the better kitchens will do a fine vegetarian spread, cheese, potatoes, pickles, rösti, that suits Indian tastes well. Warm, convivial and utterly of the place.

venues.name: Zermatt–Cervinia international ski area
venues.note: One of the largest linked ski areas in the Alps, spanning two countries, over 300km of pistes and lifts to 3,883m, so you can ski down to lunch in Italy and be back in Switzerland by tea. Long, sun-soaked, high-altitude runs with the Matterhorn always in view. A private ski guide and ski-in ski-out chalet make it seamless for a family.

venues.name: Summer glacier skiing
venues.note: The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise pistes let you ski or snowboard on real snow through July and August, a novelty few places on earth can offer, then swap boots for sandals in the valley the same day. Ideal for a summer-visiting family who want their children to touch snow in high season. The highest, largest summer ski area in the Alps.
credentials: Highest and largest summer ski area in the Alps

venues.name: Heli-skiing with Air Zermatt
venues.note: One of only a handful of legal heli-ski zones in Switzerland, where the storied Air Zermatt lifts you to untracked glacier faces such as the Monte Rosa for a guided descent through deep powder. It is the ultimate winter adrenaline day, private, exclusive and framed by the Matterhorn. For confident skiers, nothing here comes close.

venues.name: Riffelalp Resort & Europe's highest tram
venues.note: A five-star mountain resort on the Gornergrat line with a 35°C open-air pool facing the Matterhorn and a little red tram, the highest in Europe, trundling guests from the station to the door. Even non-residents can ride up for the terrace and the spa's altitude drama. A honeymoon set-piece and a rare high-altitude luxury address.

venues.name: Paragliding over Zermatt
venues.note: A tandem flight that floats you off the shoulder of the mountain and out in front of the Matterhorn itself, twenty minutes of silent, soaring perspective no cable car can give. First-timers are strapped to a seasoned pilot; the harder part is the view, not the flying. An exhilarating hour for an adventurous couple or teenager.

venues.name: Mont Cervin Palace
venues.note: The grande dame of Zermatt, open since 1852 and a Leading Hotel of the World, whose sun-terrace on the main street is the village's social heart and whose kitchens include a Michelin-starred Italian table. Even for a drink or afternoon tea it is worth stepping inside for the old-world grandeur. The classic address for a traveller who wants the establishment choice.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: CERVO Mountain Resort
venues.area: Above the village, by the Sunnegga funicular
venues.note: A cluster of chic alpine chalets with a buzzing après terrace, a superb spa and a pan-Asian and Mediterranean dining scene that draws a younger, stylish crowd. Ski-in ski-out in winter, a design-forward retreat in summer. The most fashionable stay in Zermatt for guests who want energy as well as views.

venues.name: Trockener Steg & the Theodul Glacier
venues.note: The great glacier junction where the cable cars change for the summit, ringed by the Theodul Glacier and a small lake that mirrors the Matterhorn's western flank. It is the staging point for summer skiing and the Italy crossing, worth a pause for the raw glacial scale. A window on the ice for those who go no higher.

venues.name: A guided Monte Rosa excursion
venues.note: For strong walkers, a guided crossing of the Gorner Glacier toward the striking crystalline Monte Rosa hut is a genuine high-alpine adventure without the technicality of the Matterhorn. Roped up, crampons on, you feel the scale of Switzerland's highest massif underfoot. A serious mountain day for the fit and curious, arranged privately.
credentials: Monte Rosa is the highest massif in Switzerland (Dufourspitze 4,634m)

venues.name: Winter horse-drawn sleigh & village nights
venues.note: With no cars, winter evenings belong to horse-drawn sleighs jingling through snow-lined lanes, lantern light on the old chalets and the peak silvered by the moon. A short ride to dinner or simply around the village is pure alpine romance. The car-free hush makes Zermatt's winter unlike anywhere else.

venues.name: Elsie's Bar
venues.note: A tiny champagne-and-wine room opposite the church, in an 1879 house, the chic address since 1961.

venues.name: CERVO Bar & Terrace
venues.note: A two-level slope-side terrace at the foot of Sunnegga, cocktails, DJ sets and the day's best après crowd.
credentials: Within CERVO Mountain Resort, Design Hotels (Marriott Bonvoy)

venues.name: Vernissage Bar
venues.note: Heinz Julen's cinema-cum-gallery-cum-bar, sculptural, candlelit and unlike any other room in the Alps.
credentials: Within Backstage Hotel Vernissage, MICHELIN Guide Hotel

venues.name: Hennu Stall
venues.note: The legendary slope-side après barn, Jägermeister on skis, Europop and fancy dress until the light goes.
credentials: World Snow Awards, Zermatt named Best Après-Ski
